evidence: RESULT.md §§1–2: multiplication by the denominator gives W_n-W_{n+1}=x_{n-1}x_{n+1}, with W_n=(b+1)x_n+x_{n-1}+x_{n-2}+x_{n-3}+x_{n-4}. Its sublevels bound the orbit in the closed nonnegative orthant. A positive limiting value would give a nonzero omega-limit orbit on which W is constant, but the strongly connected dependency graph has a self-loop for b>0, so a nonzero nonnegative state eventually becomes strictly positive, contradicting constant W.

RESULT.md §§2–3: for d=b+5, U_n=W_n/d is the stationary left projection of the primitive stochastic derivative. The exact drift bounds U_n-U_{n+1} by O(U_n^2), giving U_{n+k}/U_n→1 for fixed k. On the zero-projection subspace, choose k so a k-step power of the derivative has norm below 1/2. Dividing by U_{n+k}^p preserves eventual strict contraction for p=2 and p=3: the first stable error is forced by O(U_n^2); after subtracting the quadratic graph, its defect is O(U_n^3) and the stable derivative is M+O(U_n). This gives the claimed O(U_n^3) orbit remainder without assuming the decay rate.

Independent SymPy solve, with a free quadratic drift coefficient: write U'=U-qU^2+O(U^3), impose the shift equations alpha_j-alpha_{j-1}=q and (b+1)alpha_0+sum_{j=1}^4 alpha_j=0; equate the first-coordinate coefficient of U^2 from the rational map to alpha_0-q. Solving gives q=1/d and alpha_j=(jd-10)/d^2. In the exact drift the two factors then have quadratic coefficients alpha_1 and alpha_0-q, whose sum is 2alpha_0. The cubic drift coefficient is 20/d^3 and the linear-in-U reciprocal increment coefficient is 1/d^2-20/d^3=(b-15)/d^3.

RESULT.md §4: the reciprocal increment first gives U_n∼d/n, then U_n=d/n+O(log n/n^2). Subtracting 1/d+[(b-15)/d^2]log(1+1/n) from that increment leaves an absolutely summable error. Finally 1/x_n-1/U_n→-alpha_0, so the finite part is for x_n itself, not only the projected coordinate.
correctness.rationale: For every fixed b>0, at a=b+1 and with five strictly positive initial values, the recurrence is forward-defined and the asserted expansion holds: 1/x_n = n/(b+5) + [(b-15)/(b+5)^2] log n + C + o(1). The uncorrected finite part is finite precisely at b=15; it goes to minus infinity below and plus infinity above that gain. The proof supplies the global basin within the positive orthant and controls the remainder rather than relying on a formal center expansion.
validation_limits: The independent computation checks exact algebra; the global and infinite-time assertions follow from the analytic proof. The supplied checker.py was inspected, not executed. Its finite-time assertions test a tolerance for n*x_n from one constant history at each of four gains, not convergence of the printed renormalized residual.
No extension to b=0, signed histories, off-critical parameters, or estimates uniform as b approaches zero is established.
